- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–2% to reflect bearish sentiment.
- Model tends to lag in early days of a new trend (e.g., after sentiment shift); for first 3–5 days of a new trend, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast, avoiding over-smoothing.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates near the end of the forecast window; reduce final 3–5 days by 0.5–1.5% to reflect diminishing momentum or market correction.
